title: How anchors reach their lines
question: When I click a link in a chapter, how does the viewer find and scroll to the right code?
answer: Anchors are ordinary Markdown links with a #L line fragment. The checker guarantees they point at a file the chapter shows; the viewer maps the line numbers to rows, reveals them, then scrolls while remembering where you were.

chapters.title: Parse anchors from prose
chapters.body: Chapter prose is plain text. Any Markdown link whose target ends in `#L<start>-L<end>` matches [the inline pattern](src/shared/guide.ts#L55) and becomes [a typed anchor](src/shared/guide.ts#L70-L75): a file path plus a line range.

chapters.title: Reject anchors to unseen code
chapters.body:
Before anyone reads a guide, the checker requires every anchor to name [one of its chapter's excerpts](src/server/resolve.ts#L215-L218).

An anchor outside the excerpt's lines only [earns a warning](src/server/resolve.ts#L225-L227), because the viewer can expand collapsed code to reach it.

chapters.title: Map line numbers to rows
chapters.body: The viewer holds each excerpt as rows, not line numbers. [The row lookup](src/ui/lib/excerpt.ts#L16-L30) finds the rows a range covers and [pulls in removed lines](src/ui/lib/excerpt.ts#L28) just above it, so an anchor on a rewritten line also shows what it replaced.

chapters.title: Reveal, scroll, remember
chapters.body:
A click [reveals and marks the rows](src/ui/components/GuideTab.tsx#L84-L87) synchronously, so they exist before [the smooth scroll](src/ui/components/GuideTab.tsx#L70-L76) measures them.

The scroll saves the old position, which [Go back](src/ui/components/GuideTab.tsx#L97-L101) restores instantly.
